import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import json

# Load CSVs
customers = pd.read_csv('/home/user/customers.csv')
orders = pd.read_csv('/home/user/orders.csv')
items = pd.read_csv('/home/user/items.csv')

# Setup SQLite DB
conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
customers.to_sql('customers', conn, index=False)
orders.to_sql('orders', conn, index=False)
items.to_sql('items', conn, index=False)

# JOIN ensures we only get customers who have spent something.
# If we want to include everyone (even those with 0), we'd use LEFT JOIN and COALESCE.
# Given the previous script used an implicit join, it likely intended to only show customers with purchases.
query = """
SELECT c.name as customer_name, ROUND(SUM(i.price), 2) as total_spent
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN items i ON o.order_id = i.order_id
GROUP BY c.name;
"""

df_result = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)

# Ensure total_spent is float
df_result['total_spent'] = df_result['total_spent'].astype(float)

# Convert to list of dictionaries
result_list = df_result.to_dict(orient='records')

# Output to summary.json
with open('/home/user/summary.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(result_list, f, indent=2)

print("Processing complete. Results saved to /home/user/summary.json")
EOF

cat /home/user/summary.json
